newsitem.title: USA: TWA's first quarter loss grows.
newsitem.headline: TWA's first quarter loss grows.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc., reporting an expected first-quarter loss, said Monday it finished the period "ahead of plan" and anticipated that certain costs would decline in the second and third quarters.

"First-quarter results reflect certain unusual costs -- including an accelerated narrow-body maintenance schedule and training costs associated with the phase-out of our larger wide-body aircraft -- that will decline as we move into the second and third quarters," said Chief Executive Gerald Gitner.
The airline said it lost $71.6 million, or $1.54 a share, for the quarter, compared with a year-earlier loss of $37.1 million, or $1.46 a share.
TWA reported quarterly revenue of $762.3 million, down from $782.4 million a year earlier.
"The reduced revenue reflected a planned reduction in capacity resulting from the ongoing replacement of 747 and L1011 aircraft with smaller 767 and 757 aircraft," the company said.
"TWA also reduced the number of narrow-body aircraft in its schedule to move more aircraft through required scheduled maintenance prior to the peak travel season," TWA said.
Separately, TWA said it cut fares on round trip domestic flights from 11 U.S. and Canadian cities and on flights to five international cities from New York.
The lowest domestic fares are available Tuesday, Wednesday and Saturday and the domestic fare sale ends April 25.
The international fares are discounted up to 39 percent and that sale ends April 28, TWA said.
TWA said its operating expenses for the quarter climbed to $861.8 million from $836.6 million as the average cost per gallon of jet fuel rose to 74.02 cents from 66.58 a year ago.
Quarterly system-wide passenger load factor was 66.3 percent, up from 63.6 percent a year ago, TWA said.

Quarterly revenue per available seat mile was 8.75 cents, up from 8.31 cents. Quarterly average yield per revenue passenger mile was 11.84 cents, up from 11.59 cents. Quarterly operating expense per available seat mile was 9.86 cents, compared with 8.82 cents a year ago.
TWA stock was up 50 cents at $7.125 in morning trading on the American Stock Exchange.
